newsitem.title: CHINA: China collects $4.44 bln in farm taxes in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China collects $4.44 bln in farm taxes in 1996.

text.p: China collected 36.88 billion yuan ($4.44 billion) in agricultural taxes in 1996, up 33.2 percent from 1995, the China Taxation News said on Wednesday.

State tax income from general farming and herding rose a year-on-year 42.4 percent in 1996 to 18.26 billion yuan, the newspaper said, quoting Xu Jiatong, director of the agricultural tax bureau under the State General Administration of Taxation.

Revenue from special agricultural products climbed 35.5 percent year on year to 13.11 billion yuan in 1996, but that from the use of arable land fell 9.7 percent to 3.01 billion yuan over the same period, Xu said.
Agrigultural taxes accounted for less than three percent of farmers' average income, Xu said but gave no further details.
Beijing, worried that heavy fees levied on farmers could lead to social unrest, has said taxes on those who till the land must not exceed five percent of their incomes.
